package_info.why_malicious: The package is considered malicious because it contains code that conditionally executes only in specific customer web environments, enabling targeted attacks against the banking sector. The attackers used advanced evasion techniques, such as environment-aware execution and customized command and control infrastructure, to exfiltrate sensitive browser data or perform unauthorized actions, making detection and attribution more difficult.

execution_context.trigger: At runtime, when the application is loaded in a browser environment
execution_context.file_location: Main application code (exact file not specified in report)
required_permissions: network access (to make outbound HTTP requests)
access to browser environment variables (window.location, document.cookie, window.localStorage)

malicious_snippets.code_behavior: At runtime, the code checks if the browser's window.location.hostname matches a targeted domain, then exfiltrates sensitive browser data (cookies and localStorage) via an outbound HTTPS POST request to a custom command and control server, resulting in targeted data theft from specific banking environments.

malice_analysis.why_suspicious: This code is suspicious because it conditionally executes only when loaded on a specific customer domain, and then exfiltrates sensitive browser data (cookies, localStorage) to an external, attacker-controlled server. Such targeted, environment-aware exfiltration is a hallmark of advanced supply chain attacks.
malice_analysis.violated_expectations: Legitimate open-source packages should not contain code that checks for specific customer domains or exfiltrates sensitive browser data to external servers. Code that accesses cookies and localStorage and sends them to unknown domains is a clear violation of user privacy and security expectations.
malice_analysis.similar_legitimate_use: Conditional code execution based on environment is sometimes used for feature toggling, A/B testing, or analytics, but never for exfiltrating sensitive data such as cookies or localStorage to non-affiliated domains.
key_indicators: Conditional execution based on window.location.hostname matching a specific domain
Access and exfiltration of document.cookie and window.localStorage
Outbound HTTPS POST requests to custom, non-standard domains (e.g., custom-c2.example.com)
Presence of code that only activates in targeted customer environments

attack_chain.action: Malicious package is installed as a dependency in the target's web application, either directly or via a compromised supply chain.
attack_chain.leads_to: Malicious code is present in the production environment and will be executed in end-user browsers.

attack_chain.action: At runtime, the code checks if it is running in a specific customer web environment by evaluating window.location.hostname (e.g., targetbank.com).
attack_chain.leads_to: If the condition is met, the malicious payload is executed only for users of the targeted domain.

attack_chain.action: The malicious payload exfiltrates sensitive browser data (cookies, localStorage) to a customized command and control server controlled by the attacker.
attack_chain.leads_to: Attacker receives sensitive data from users of the targeted banking environment, enabling further compromise or fraud.

behavioral_signatures: Conditional execution of code based on window.location.hostname or similar environment checks targeting specific domains
Access and exfiltration of browser storage data (document.cookie, window.localStorage) at runtime
Outbound network requests (e.g., fetch, XMLHttpRequest) to non-standard or dynamically generated domains
file_indicators: Presence of code that checks for specific customer domains using window.location.hostname or equivalent
Code that accesses both document.cookie and window.localStorage in close proximity
Obfuscated or dynamically generated network request code targeting external domains
network_indicators: Outbound HTTPS POST requests to attacker-controlled or unusual domains (e.g., custom-c2.example.com)
Custom command and control endpoints that are unique per target or customer environment
detection_knowledge.how_to_detect: Use static and dynamic analysis to identify code in dependencies that conditionally executes based on the runtime environment (such as window.location.hostname checks). Flag any code that accesses and exfiltrates browser data (cookies, localStorage) to non-standard or unknown domains. Monitor network traffic for outbound HTTPS POST requests to custom or suspicious domains, and correlate with code that only activates in specific customer environments. Automated detection should prioritize environment-aware payloads and data exfiltration patterns.
